title: Create `frame_num_t` type
description:
Based on a [discussion on Discord][1], create a type `frame_num_t` for
holding a frame number. Meant mostly for self-documenting code, but also
potentially helpful in the future if we want to support more than
`G_MAXUINT32` packets in a single capture.

As an example use case, if a number is going to be set from or assigned
to `pinfo->num`, then it is a candidate for having this type.

Define `FRAME_NUM_MAX` to be the largest frame number we can support.
Again, potentially useful for increasing the number of frames in a
capture.

Define `FRAME_NUM_UNKNOWN` to be 0, and use that in a few token cases.
This is probably less important of a change, though it does drive home
that our frame numbers start from 1 and not 0 like most C structures.

This does not currently replace all cases where it "should" be used.
(I only got about a third of the way through searching epan for
the word "frame".)
I've probably put more time into this than warranted for a MR that may
not even be accepted. If there is interest then I can continue.

[1]: https://discord.com/channels/889214182837321788/889214225145266288/1092382690323464214

notes.body: I'm a bit curious how we can ensure we cover all places this type should be used. I know some dissectors which does not use the word "frame" in variables which should use this type. Maybe make `frame_num_t` a type which is not compatible with `guint32` and let the compiler tell you?
